claims.claim: Broadly, rhythm concerns the durations of musical sounds and rests in time.
In the cited introductory text, beat is described as a basic unit or consistent pulse, while tempo is the speed at which that beat occurs.
The cited text distinguishes meter from beat by describing meter as the grouping of beats and notes stronger and weaker positions within the grouping.
Common Western notation represents note and rest values hierarchically, with each common note value divisible into two smaller values.
In the cited notation text, a dot adds half of a note's original duration and a tie joins same-pitch notes without a new articulation of the tied-to notes.
Syncopation can arise when timing or accent challenges a perceived metrical hierarchy, including through rests or ties in the cited discussion.
Rhythm and meter can be taught from basic notation through broader analytical and style-specific topics, so this lesson should distinguish the concepts rather than collapse them.
